clue.text: Tree of Life scarf held up by attractive young woman briefly

indicators.note: in a down clue, something held up is lifted so it reads from bottom to top
said briefly, a word is cut short by losing its final letter
a thing held is gripped inside something else, here inside the young woman

blocks.note: a babe is slang for an attractive young woman
a boa is a long fluffy scarf

explanation.surface: A fashionable young woman lifts her scarf on a tree that sustains life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' trims the young woman before the upturned scarf goes inside her.
explanation.definitionFit: The African baobab stores huge amounts of water and supplies food, so it is popularly nicknamed the Tree of Life.

clue.text: Insightful comment made when disposable item has part removed from both ends

indicators.text: has part removed from both ends
indicators.note: a piece is cut off each end of the item, so its first and last letters go

blocks.note: a paper cup is thrown away after one use

explanation.surface: Someone makes a sharp remark while a throwaway object is trimmed at each end.
explanation.walkthrough: PAPER CUP loses its outer P and P to leave APERCU.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperçu, borrowed from French, is a brief illuminating observation or quick perceptive summary.

clue.text: Ex-PM informally to express disapproval when judge interferes

indicators.note: one who interferes gets in among things, so the judge goes into the middle

blocks.note: to boo is to jeer in disapproval
J is the standard abbreviation for judge

explanation.surface: A former prime minister is jeered when a judge steps into his affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: BoJo is the tabloid nickname of Boris Johnson, British prime minister from 2019 to 2022.

clue.text: Skilled worker dismisses writer as president

indicators.note: to dismiss someone is to send them away, so the writer's letters leave the worker

blocks.note: a carpenter is a skilled woodworker
a pen is something that writes

explanation.surface: A tradesman sacks an author who has become head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: CARPENTER without PEN leaves CARTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Jimmy Carter served as the thirty-ninth US head of state, from 1977 to 1981.

clue.text: Just over half of mathematical subject ultimately taught throughout American city

indicators.note: keeping a little more than half a word means the rest of its letters are dropped
ultimately means in the end, so only the final letters are wanted

blocks.note: calculus is a branch of mathematics
the last letter of taught
the last letter of throughout
A is a standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A maths course is partly taught in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: Five of the eight letters of CALCULUS is just over half, giving CALCU; 'ultimately' applies to both taught and throughout.
explanation.definitionFit: Calcutta, now officially Kolkata, is a major Indian metropolis on the Hooghly river.

clue.text: He painted endless group of camels going astray with at first none missing

indicators.note: without an end, the group of camels loses its last letter
at first points to the opening letter of the following word only
with that letter missing, it is taken away from the other word
letters going astray wander out of their proper order

blocks.note: a caravan is a train of camels crossing a desert
taken as written
the first letter of none, which is the letter taken out

explanation.surface: A desert train of camels wanders off, though not one animal is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: CARAVAN loses its end to give CARAVA; GOING without N leaves GOIG, rearranged as GGIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Caravaggio was the Italian Baroque master famed for dramatic light and shadow, so he is someone who painted.

clue.text: German newspaper format

blocks.note: first meaning: a person from the German capital
second meaning: a mid-sized page format between tabloid and broadsheet

explanation.surface: A paper from Germany is described by its page layout.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a native of Berlin and also a page size used by papers such as Le Monde.

clue.text: Bit of exquisite taste he developed?

definitions.text: Bit of exquisite taste he developed?

indicators.note: a bit of a word is just one letter of it, here its first
something developed has been worked into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the opening letter of exquisite
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man of refined palate has cultivated a touch of exquisite taste.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the person who developed exquisite taste.
explanation.definitionFit: An aesthete is a person with a cultivated appreciation of art and beauty, someone with refined sensibilities.

clue.text: Vessel's active measure of speed or acceleration

blocks.note: A is the grammatical abbreviation for active
miles per hour
taken as written
a is the physics symbol for acceleration

explanation.surface: A ship's specification lists its speed or acceleration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship with a top speed, but it is a jar.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphora is a tall two-handled ancient Greek or Roman jar for wine or oil.

clue.text: Expert made changes inside university, say

indicators.note: the word made undergoes changes, so its letters are reordered
inside places the altered letters within the expert

blocks.note: an ace is a highly skilled person
made rearranged

explanation.surface: A specialist has introduced reforms at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expert made changes' reads as a sentence, but 'made' is the word being altered.
explanation.definitionFit: Academe is the world of scholarship and higher learning, of which a university is one instance.

clue.text: Vessel involved in fight, an extremely stressful situation

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be caught up within it

blocks.note: a bout is a boxing or wrestling match
an urn is a vase-like container

explanation.surface: A pot gets caught up in a brawl, which is very stressful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a container for ashes or tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Burnout is collapse from prolonged overwork, a state brought on by relentless pressure and exhaustion.

clue.text: Little man's headgear?

blocks.note: surface reading: a hat for a small fellow
setter's reading: a word for a fellow plus a diminutive ending, like piglet, also names a garland worn on the head

explanation.surface: A question about what a short chap wears on his head.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplet is a wreath or circlet of flowers worn on the head, so it is literally headgear.

clue.text: Forest fruit railway destroyed starts to emotionally trouble UN soldier

indicators.note: the railway is destroyed, so it is wiped out of the fruit
the starts of words are their first letters

blocks.note: a blueberry is a woodland berry
RY is the abbreviation for railway
the first letters of emotionally and trouble

explanation.surface: A peacekeeper is upset to find berries and a wrecked railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: BLUEBERRY minus RY gives BLUEBER, followed by ET.
explanation.definitionFit: United Nations peacekeepers wear distinctive pale blue headwear, so a blue beret is the nickname for one.

clue.text: A boy upset about tense facial feature

indicators.note: about means turned around and in disorder, so the letters before it are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A distressed lad worries about something on his face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the letters to rearrange; 'about' does the shuffling.
explanation.definitionFit: A beauty spot is a small dark mole on the cheek, once thought attractive and sometimes painted on.

clue.text: Broadway show news that is written on the first of April

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of April
read as new's, the plural of N for new
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for that is

explanation.surface: A theatre announcement is made on April Fool's Day.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'written on' means placed after, so the other pieces follow the first letter of April.
explanation.definitionFit: Annie is the 1977 musical about an orphan, a long-running hit on the New York stage.

clue.text: Musical giant finally wanting hot stuff for dessert

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, and finally points to the last letter that is lacking

blocks.note: J S Bach is a towering figure of music
lava is molten rock

explanation.surface: A great composer wants something spicy for pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: BACH without its last letter gives BAC, then LAVA.
explanation.definitionFit: Baclava, more often spelt baklava, is a sweet pastry of filo layers, nuts and honey syrup served after a meal.

clue.text: Reversing taxi in front of vehicle with a trailer, initially a game of luck

indicators.note: a reversing vehicle goes backwards, so the word is read from end to start
initially points to the first letter of trailer alone

blocks.note: a cab is a taxi
a car is a vehicle
taken as written
the opening letter of trailer

explanation.surface: A taxi backs up ahead of a car towing a trailer.
explanation.definitionFit: Baccarat is a casino card game where players bet on which hand wins, decided largely by chance.

clue.text: Possibly German internet domain facing difficult problem

blocks.note: .com is the commercial internet domain
a poser is a puzzling question

explanation.surface: A German website has run into a tricky snag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German' looks like a nationality, but it is Sir Edward German, the English writer of light operas.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward German wrote Merrie England and other music, so he is one example of a creator of musical works.

clue.text: One consuming soft drink died but gets strong praise

indicators.note: something consuming another takes it inside, as if swallowing it

blocks.note: an ace counts as one in cards and dice
cola is a fizzy drink
d is the abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: Someone who drinks a soda dies yet is showered with tributes.
explanation.walkthrough: The ace in cards and dice counts as one, which is why it can stand for the word.
explanation.definitionFit: An accolade is an award or expression of high esteem, a formal tribute to achievement.

clue.text: Motorhome's stuck in aquatic plants in holiday destination

indicators.note: something stuck in a place is lodged within it

blocks.note: algae are simple water plants
RV stands for recreational vehicle

explanation.surface: A camper van gets bogged down in pondweed on the way to a resort.
explanation.walkthrough: RV goes inside ALGAE: ALGA(RV)E; the 's on Motorhome stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Algarve is Portugal's southern coastal region, famous for beaches and package tourism.

clue.text: Roughly 55% income tax for space traveller

indicators.note: a little over half of a phrase is kept, the run of letters at its centre

blocks.note: five letters from the middle of these nine, which is about 55 per cent

explanation.surface: A hefty rate of income tax is levied on an astronaut.
explanation.walkthrough: Five of nine letters is 55.5 per cent, hence 'roughly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A comet is an icy body that journeys through the solar system on a long orbit around the sun.

clue.text: Part of theatre in which 200 see captivating unknown play (with no director)

indicators.note: to captivate is to hold captive, so the unknown is held within
the abbreviation for director is removed from the play

blocks.note: CC is 200 in Roman numerals
y is an algebraic unknown
lo is an old word meaning look or see
a drama is a play

explanation.surface: A theatre stages an obscure play watched by two hundred people, without any director.
explanation.walkthrough: Lo is an old exclamation meaning look, as in 'lo and behold'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyclorama is the large curved backdrop at the rear of a stage, often lit to suggest sky.

clue.text: Rachel Reeves ignores rollover opportunity

indicators.note: turned over in a down clue, the word is flipped to read backwards
what is ignored is left out of the title

blocks.note: Rachel Reeves became Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer, its finance minister, in 2024
the first four letters of this word, before the indicator inside it

explanation.surface: The British finance minister passes up the chance of a rollover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rollover' reads as one financial word, but it splits into roll plus a turning signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A chance is an opening or favourable occasion to do something, the same as an opportunity.

clue.text: Relative's name written in stone

indicators.note: something written in a surface is set within it, like an inscription

blocks.note: agate is a banded gemstone
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A family member's name is carved on a gravestone.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnate is a kinsman descended through the male line, a paternal blood connection.

clue.text: Quickly injecting heroin - that's brave

indicators.note: injecting puts one thing into another, so the drug goes inside

blocks.note: apace means swiftly
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A drug user hurriedly shoots up and calls it courageous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' looks like an adjective, but it is the noun for a Native American warrior. H goes inside APACE.
explanation.definitionFit: An Apache warrior is one example of a brave, the older term for a Native American fighting man.

clue.text: Excitement as noisy party leader is deposed

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, and deposing it removes it

blocks.note: a carousal is a drunken, rowdy celebration

explanation.surface: A loud political party gets thrilled as its chief is overthrown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests politics, a reading the deposed leader supports, but it is a revel.
explanation.definitionFit: Arousal is a state of heightened stimulation or stirred feeling, the same as excitement.

clue.text: Two parts of the UK, one country

blocks.note: ALBA is the Gaelic name for Scotland and NI is Northern Ireland
a means one

explanation.surface: Two regions of Britain are combined into a single nation.
explanation.walkthrough: ALBA and NI are the two parts, followed by A.
explanation.definitionFit: Albania is a Balkan republic on the Adriatic coast, with Tirana as its capital.

clue.text: Singer-songwriter regularly visited bordello

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A musician made regular trips to a brothel.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Brel was the Belgian chansonnier who wrote and performed Ne me quitte pas.

clue.text: Barometer's software package requiring a different key

indicators.note: one musical key letter is swapped out for another

blocks.note: Android is Google's mobile operating system

explanation.surface: A weather gauge's software needs another password.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' suggests a password or keyboard, but D and E are both musical keys: ANDROID with E for D.
explanation.definitionFit: An aneroid is a barometer measuring air pressure with a sealed metal box rather than liquid.

clue.text: Intensely dislike revolutionary chasing red cat

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: Che Guevara was the archetypal communist, or red
to hate is to dislike intensely

explanation.surface: A radical who loathes communists pursues them, like a hunting cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' wants to be Che, but it reverses HATE; Che comes from 'red'. Chasing means coming after.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheetah is the spotted African big cat, the fastest land animal.
